newsitem.title: USA: LADWP board approves partner, plan goes to city.
newsitem.headline: LADWP board approves partner, plan goes to city.

text.p: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power's (LADWP) board of commissioners unanimously approved on Tuesday a staff recommendation for a "strategic partnership" with Duke-Louis Dreyfus.
Duke-Dreyfus, a joint venture of North Carolina utility Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp, was the winner of a nearly year-long selection process.
The alliance must still be reviewed by the Los Angeles City Council, which LADWP commissioners on Tuesday hoped would happen soon.
William McCarley, LADWP general manager, said the next meeting of an ad hoc committee established by the council to review electricity restructuring would be February 20.
He suggested the city council may review the proposal shortly after that meeting.
Simon Rich, co-chairman of Duke-Dreyfus, said the firm would be able to establish a trading floor in Los Angeles within 4 to 6 weeks of final approval.
He stressed that Duke-Dreyfus will be especially valuable to LADWP in managing volatility of energy markets as utilities exit the era of regulated returns and enter competition.
William Louis-Dreyfus, the other co-chairman of the joint venture, said the interests of both partners were equal.
"We come with no vested interests to protect," he added.
